title: From opening the page to reading a folder
description: What the page shows from the moment it opens, including every message the status line can give on the way. Each state is a screen a design has to cover.

states.description: The page has loaded, asks /auth/me whether a Worker serves it and signs readers in, and looks for ?url= in its address. Nothing is shown yet.

The landing page: headline, what the browser does, the address field with Browse, an example repository, a note on tokens and a tile for each of the ten kinds of view. The bar shows only the brand. Under the address field, Sign in with GitHub (optional): on the Worker with include my private repositories, without it a field for a GitHub token. Signed in, it says who they are, with Sign out, and the address field gets a drop-down of their repositories; after a failed or cancelled sign-in it says so in red.
The bar shows the repository's name; the status line reads 'Listing owner/repository on GitHub…' with a small square that ticks round. Nothing else is shown.

The status line, in red: 'Couldn't list the repository.' and why: the address is not a repository, the host refused the token, the token does not cover the repository, GitHub's 60 requests an hour are used up, no such repository or it is private, or no such branch, tag or commit. After a 401, 403 or 404 a button offers 'Add a token', or 'Replace or add a token'. The button after it is Sign in with GitHub, or Include private repositories, for a GitHub repository on the Worker; elsewhere Add a token, or Replace or add a token.

The status line, in red: the repository (or folder) 'has no views or knowledge files in' .dev/*.json (or .cyberspace-explorer/ where the root has it) 'at' its ref, and that the skills describe how to add them.
The bar adds the ref as a pill; the status line reads 'Reading N view and knowledge files…' with the ticking square.

The folder column and the folder view. The status line is empty, or notes that the repository was too large to list in full, which files were skipped and why, or that the drawing library couldn't load and views are shown as tables.
The Waiting view in place of a folder: open decisions and blockers across the repository. The Waiting link in the folder column is marked.

Cyberspace in place of the folder column and the view: a sky and a ground grid under the bar, with the status line floating over them. On a first entry the status line reads 'Loading Cyberspace's 3D library…' with the ticking square; if the WebGL context is lost it reads 'The 3D view stopped.' with a Restore it button.
